genes.description: Efficiency and speed of aquatic movement. High expression enables deep-sea and open-ocean colonization.
Speed and endurance on terrestrial terrain. Critical for escaping predators and covering large home ranges.
Ability to achieve and sustain powered flight. Opens access to aerial and cliff terrain.
Ability to excavate and inhabit underground tunnels. Provides shelter and access to subsurface food.
Arboreal movement and grip strength. Enables exploitation of forest canopy niches.
Preference and adaptation for consuming animal tissue. High expression increases predation efficiency but requires prey population.
Adaptation for digesting plant material. Expands enormously with terrestrial plant colonization.
Dietary flexibility to consume both plant and animal matter. Provides resilience when one food source declines.
Ability to extract plankton and microorganisms from water. Very efficient in nutrient-rich marine zones.
Detritivore ability — consuming dead organic matter. Primarily relevant for Fungi kingdom species.
Specialization in consuming floral nectar. Enables mutualistic pollination relationships with plant species.
Speed of population recovery. High expression enables rapid recovery after population crashes.
Number of offspring produced per reproductive cycle. High clutch = high population ceiling but more resource demand.
Investment in offspring survival after birth. High expression trades quantity for quality — fewer but more viable young.
Ability to reproduce without a mate. Powerful colonizer trait — allows single individual to found a new population.
Physical protection via exoskeleton, shell, or dermal armor. Reduces predation loss but increases metabolic cost.
Chemical defense via venom, poison, or noxious secretions. Deters predators and can be used offensively.
Visual concealment in the environment. Reduces both predation risk and prey detection — dual-edged trait.
Coordinated pack, herd, or colony behavior for mutual protection. Scales with population size — stronger when populous.
Ability to regrow lost tissue or limbs. Reduces mortality from injury.
Sharpness and range of visual detection. Critical for both predators and prey in open terrain.
Sound-based navigation and prey detection. Effective in dark, dense, or aquatic environments.
Detection of electric fields generated by muscle contractions. Dominant sense in murky aquatic environments.
Sensitivity to chemical signals — smell and taste. Used for prey detection, mate finding, and territory marking.
Pressure wave detection system in aquatic species. Enables schooling behavior and detecting approaching threats.
Ability to survive and function in cold environments. Required to colonize Tundra and IceSheet terrain.
Resistance to high temperatures and arid conditions. Required to colonize Desert terrain.
Internal heat regulation — warm-bloodedness. Enables activity in cold climates but requires far higher food intake.
Ability to enter dormancy during food-scarce cold periods. Dramatically reduces winter mortality.
